$comment: Intended differences between the Next.js baseline and the bespoke build.
Every rule needs a `reason`. `pattern` and `routes` are substrings, or
`re:<javascript regexp>`. `kind` is head | prose | code | text | html | file.
diff-html.ts prints rules that matched nothing, so stale entries surface.
Titles on /blog/<slug> and /notes/<slug> are a DELIBERATE deviation from
the baseline, decided by the coordinator: posts and notes now get the
'%s | Max Leiter' template of CONTRACT item 14. It fixes two Next defects
at once, since generateMetadata skipped the template and notes/[slug]
exported no metadata at all, leaving all 8 note pages sharing the single
title 'Notes | Max Leiter'. Index and static page titles must still match
the baseline exactly, so the rule below is scoped to slug routes.
Note pages no longer lose their meta description: they inherit the
notes-layout description, exactly as the baseline does. No rule needed.
Deliberately NOT ignored, so they keep failing until fixed: the tweet card
chrome on /blog/seeing-the-future (defect, core restoring the full card

informationalReasons.text: A line diff of all visible text cannot tell code-block re-lineation from content loss: bright wrapped each fence line in a div and emitted the whole fence twice, once per theme, with one copy hidden by CSS; shiki emits it once with CSS custom properties. Superseded by two blocking streams that split the problem: prose (running text with <pre> subtracted out) and code (the ordered list of code blocks, per-theme duplicates collapsed). Kept on as printed reference.
informationalReasons.html: Phase 1 is a reimplementation: different class names, different nesting, islands instead of client components. A line diff of the markup is reference material, not a gate. The gates are head, prose, code and file.

rules.reason: The 404 page was redesigned. The baseline emitted two <title> tags ('404: This page could not be found.' and 'Max Leiter'); the new one emits '404 | Max Leiter' plus a description, a canonical and robots noindex,nofollow.
Same 404 redesign: 'This page could not be found.' became 'That page does not exist. Go home.'

Embed variants lose the breadcrumb toolbar text (the section name and the slug), which is the point of the embed route. In the baseline ?embed=true served byte-identical HTML and stripped the toolbar with a client script, so the words were still in the markup. Broad by design: every embed page's article body is checked strictly through its canonical twin, which stores the shared baseline.

A line diff of a 350 KB XML file is not a useful gate. Verified at item level instead: 48 items became 38, the 10 removed are exactly the published:false posts and notes (design doc 9.5), none were added, external posts survive, and channel title/description/link/language/atom:link are identical. Three intended body changes account for the rest: lastBuildDate is pinned to the newest item's date instead of build time, which makes the build reproducible; description links no longer carry target/rel attributes; and raw <Image .../> JSX no longer leaks into item bodies, because bodies now go through the real MDX pipeline instead of marked.
Verified at URL level: the new sitemap adds /blog, /labs, /notes and /talks, the four top-level pages the baseline omitted, and loses nothing. The rest of the diff is element formatting.

A fix. The baseline returned 404 here because the OG route fetched posts/<slug>.mdx from GitHub at request time and this post's file is introducing-HFSViewer.mdx. The new build prerenders it locally at 1200x630 like the other 23.
Fonts moved from /_next/static/media to /_assets and are preloaded by hand. The baseline's equivalent preloads pointed at /_next/ and are stripped by the normalizer, so only the added lines show.
The single inline stylesheet moved position within <head>. Its content is deliberately not compared; see the note in normalize-html.ts.
The new blocking theme script required by CONTRACT. Pinned to its exact content hash, so any change to the script fails the run.
A Next-specific meta tag with no equivalent in the bespoke build.
Next emitted an extra preloaded stylesheet link on some routes; the bespoke build inlines all CSS instead.
Posts and notes are now og:type=article. The baseline said website on every page, articles included.
Added for articles per CONTRACT Head.publishedTime. The baseline emitted no published time anywhere.
The RSS alternate link is now on every page. The baseline had it only on the homepage, because pages setting alternates.canonical dropped the inherited alternates.types.
Corrected from 600 to 630. Every OG PNG has always been 1200x630; the baseline metadata mis-declared the height.
The same 600 to 630 correction as og:image:height.
Dropped. Not a tag the Twitter card spec defines, and og:image:type carries the same information.
Now emitted consistently on every page. The baseline emitted it only on pages that set a per-page OG image.
Embed variants are now noindex,nofollow. In the baseline ?embed=true served byte-identical HTML with 'index, follow', so every post was indexable at two URLs.
The same noindex,nofollow fix as meta[name=robots] on embed variants.
The notes index and all 8 note pages had no canonical at all in the baseline. The href prefix is pinned, so a canonical pointing anywhere else still fails.
The homepage had no canonical in the baseline. Pinned to the exact expected value.

Intended. React 19 auto-preloads any without loading="lazy", which is how the baseline got 24 of these across 7 posts. The bespoke build marks only the first article image eager with fetchpriority=high and lazy-loads the rest, so the LCP image is still prioritised without 23 competing eager fetches. Note that Change.line carries no +/- sign, so this rule hides added preloads as well as removed ones; that is intentional here, since the first-image preload is the new build's own.

Deliberate deviation from the baseline, decided by the coordinator: posts and notes get CONTRACT item 14's '%s | Max Leiter' template. Fixes two Next defects, since generateMetadata skipped the template on posts and notes/[slug] exported no metadata at all, giving all 8 note pages the identical title 'Notes | Max Leiter'. Scoped to slug routes and their embed variants, so index and static page titles must still match the baseline exactly.

rules.pattern: content="Short-form thoughts, code snippets, and tips."
rules.reason: Baseline side of the per-note description change. The baseline gave all 8 notes this one notes-layout string, because notes/[slug] exports no metadata at all. The 4 notes with no frontmatter description still fall back to it, so only 4 routes drop it.

rules.pattern: re:content="(A script for concatenating files in a directory for copying to an LLM|a bash script for generating branch names|SWR for state management|hint: just use `sql` and COALESCE\.)"
rules.reason: New side of the same change: the 4 notes that do have a frontmatter description now use it, which the coordinator decided is an intended improvement. Pinned to those exact 4 strings rather than matching any description, so a note silently falling back to a generic string still fails. If a note's frontmatter description is edited this rule goes unused, diff-html reports it as stale, and the new value shows up for review.

$allowNewRoutesComment: Matched against 'route added by new build' and against built pages that
route discovery never reached. Anything not listed here fails, so a page
appearing out of nowhere cannot go unnoticed.
Checked before allowlisting: the six list-page embeds strip the toolbar,
carry the right titles, and are noindex,nofollow. /knightos/ is the
KnightOS emulator, copied verbatim out of public/ with its own index.html,
so it is an asset rather than a route the site generates.
